title: Operator Briefing Card Library and Incident Deck Templates
author: Marcus Liu
body:
Summary

This page is a living library of one-page operator briefing cards and a reusable incident-deck template for platform-level and tenant-impacting incidents. The goal is to give on-call engineers and SREs a minimal, consistent, and actionable view for rapid triage and communication. Each briefing card is designed to be readable in 60–90 seconds and pairs a compact dashboard widget definition with a prescriptive action checklist.

When to use these cards

- Pre-incident: run a short review before high-traffic events (e.g., Black Friday, major product launches).
- During incident response: attach the appropriate card to the incident ticket and include the matching dashboard widget(s) in the incident channel.
- Post-incident and retrospectives: use the card as the canonical source for metrics referenced in the writeup.

Card structure (standardized)

Each card in the library follows this structure:

1) Title and one-line purpose (what the card is for).
2) Quick health summary (green/amber/red with current metric snapshot).
3) Key indicators (metrics and thresholds).
4) Rapid triage checklist (first 10 minutes, first 30 minutes).
5) Escalation & owners (who to call and when).
6) Short remediation playbook (safe rollbacks, fail-open/fail-closed choices).
7) Dashboard widget reference (small JSON snippet to render the widget).
8) Communication templates (Slack, customer-facing status wording).

Operator briefing card: "KV prefix cache pressure (regional)"

Purpose:
A succinct operator card for regional KV prefix cache pressure that commonly causes tail token latency and cold-start cascades for multi-tenant model serving.

Quick health snapshot:
- Status: AMBER
- Region: us-east-1
- Affected tenants: flagged by tenant-safety-score > 0.6
- Current tail P95 token-latency: 3.8s (SLO: 1.0s)

Key indicators and thresholds:
- KV cache eviction rate > 1k evictions/min -> WARNING
- Cache hit ratio < 78% for warmset -> WARNING
- Active continuous-batch queue length > 120 -> CRITICAL
- Model variant fallback rate > 2% -> WARNING

Rapid triage checklist (first 10 mins):
1. Verify alert sources: open dashboard -> top panel (see widget JSON below).
2. Confirm region and tenant subset (use tenant-filter quick link).
3. Check recent scheduler rebalances or host churn in the last 15m.
4. If eviction rate spiked, capture a heap-snapshot and heatset affinity table.
5. Post initial summary in #platform-incident (include TL;DR + observed metrics).

Rapid triage checklist (first 30 mins):
1. If active queue length is CRITICAL, initiate soft-shed policy for non-critical tenants (runbook link).
2. Consider bumping warmset priority for high-SLA tenants via runtime API:

API example:

```
# increase warmset weight for tenant abc-123
curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/api/v1/operators/warmset-adjust \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"abc-123","priority_delta":12}'
```

3. Open a tenant-impact channel and tag SEs for top customers.
4. If churn persists after 20 minutes, prepare model-variant-swap (see emergency-model-swap runbook).

Owners & escalation policy:
- Primary: runtime-ops (oncall: @runtime-ops)
- Secondary: serving-scheduler (oncall: @scheduler)
- Pager threshold: active queue length > 200 or tail P99 token-latency > 6s -> PagerDuty P0.

Short remediation playbook:
- 0−15m: soft-shed low-priority tenants, bump warmset weights for VIPs, collect diagnostics.
- 15−45m: invoke regional eviction throttle (operator CLI), start a controlled warmset rehydrate job.
- >45m: plan cross-region traffic steer to fallback region and trigger full model-variant swap if necessary.

Dashboard widget (compact JSON example)

```
{
  "title": "KV-cache-pressure: us-east-1 (brief)",
  "type": "time_series",
  "series": [
    {"metric": "kv.evictions_per_min", "label": "evictions/min", "agg": "sum"},
    {"metric": "kv.hit_ratio_warmset", "label": "hit_ratio", "agg": "avg", "yAxis": 2}
  ],
  "range": "15m",
  "thresholds": [
    {"metric": "kv.evictions_per_min", "warn": 1000, "critical": 2000},
    {"metric": "kv.hit_ratio_warmset", "warn": 0.78, "critical": 0.70}
  ]
}
```

Alert-to-card mapping table

| Alert name | Trigger | Mapped card | Immediate action | Pager? | Primary owner |
|------------|---------|-------------|------------------|--------|---------------|
| KV_EVICT_HIGH | evictions/min > 1k | KV prefix cache pressure (regional) | Check warmset hit ratio | No | runtime-ops |
| QUEUE_LEN_CRIT | queue > 120 | KV prefix cache pressure (regional) | Soft-shed non-critical tenants | Yes (P0) | runtime-ops |
| MODEL_FALLBACK_SPIKE | fallback rate > 2% | Model-variant fallback | Evaluate variant health | No | serving-release |

Communication templates

Slack short (first post):
"platform: region us-east-1 experiencing elevated KV cache evictions causing increased token latency. Impacted tenants: {short-list}. Runtime ops investigating — initial mitigation: soft-shed for low-priority tenants and warmset rehydrate. Will update in 15m."

Customer-facing status blurb (incidents page):
"We are experiencing increased latency in inference requests in our US-East region due to internal cache pressure. We are actively mitigating and expect partial restoration within 1 hour. For customers with critical SLAs we have initiated priority routing."

Incident deck template (slide outline)

- Title slide: Incident name, region, start time, lead
- TL;DR slide: scope, impact, current status (green/amber/red), immediate mitigation
- Timeline slide: event timeline with timestamps and metrics snapshots
- Root-cause candidates slide: short list of hypotheses and supporting evidence
- Actions taken slide: chronological operator actions with results (include runbook IDs)
- Customer impact & communications slide: which tenants were affected and what was communicated
- Next steps & owners slide: follow-up work, monitoring checks, retrospective date

How to onboard a service to the card library (step-by-step)

1. Service owner fills the "Card request form" and attaches a short 2‑slide summary.
2. Platform team assigns a curator (1 week) to craft metric list and thresholds.
3. Add widget JSON snippets to the dashboard repo and validate rendering in staging.
4. Run a smoke drill during next game-day to ensure the card is usable in <90s.
5. Schedule quarterly review with owners to update thresholds and owners.

Maintenance and review cadence

- Quarterly: card review with service owner and SRE curator.
- After every P0/P1 incident: update metrics and add a short postmortem note to the card.
- Annual: prune cards with no owner for >9 months.

Ownership and SLO alignment

- Each briefing card must map to at least one SLO or customer SLA. Document the exact SLI query used for SLO calculation on the card.
- Cards without SLO mapping will be deprioritized in operational runbooks.

Examples and micro-case studies (short)

1) Case: Warmset drift during hot restart (Feb 2026)
   - Symptom: gradual hit_ratio drop over 40m -> tail latency increase.
   - Action: operator bumped warmset priority and ran a rehydrate. Result: hit_ratio returned to baseline in 28m.
   - Learning: add a 1.5% guardrail on dynamic warmset-weight changes.

2) Case: Scheduler churn after erroneous kernel rollout (Nov 2025)
   - Symptom: sudden host churn and increased eviction rate.
   - Action: rollback kernel, isolate rollout cohort, invalidate affected warmsets.
   - Learning: add rollout-canary-stabilization check to preflight.

Appendix A — operator CLI quick commands

- View runtime warmset health:
```
redwoodctl runtime warmset status --region us-east-1 --json | jq '.summary'
```
- Soft-shed low-priority tenants (example):
```
redwoodctl runtime tenant set-quota --selector 'priority:low' --max-qps 0.5
```
- Start rehydrate job:
```
redwoodctl runtime warmset rehydrate --tenant abc-123 --speed fast --trace-id incident-2026-03
```

Appendix B — widget JSON best practices

- Keep widget time range to 5–30m for on-call brevity.
- Always include absolute thresholds and show last sample timestamp.
- Provide a minimal chart with max 2 series; link to full panels for deeper investigation.

Appendix C — links and runbooks

- Emergency model swap runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026.json
- KV cache rehydrate operator runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/preemptible-workload-graceful-handback-and-notification-playbook-2026.json
- Incident deck template (Google Slides): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/incident-deck-template

If you are adding a new card or updating thresholds, ping @runtime-ops and attach a short justification for the change. Cards are intentionally conservative: prefer clear actionability over comprehensive metric lists.
